attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The unproved gap is the same-theory trace modulus outside the mirror-smooth core. Current RG compactness estimates may control separated reflected probes, but they do not yet rule out reflection-plane contact terms, Wilson-loop cusp/intersection renormalization, or composite-operator boundary mixing as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
steps: Start with finite \(F_1,\ldots,F_N\in\mathcal A_+\) and coefficients \(c\). For each \(\delta>0\), set \(F_i^\delta=T_\delta F_i\), so all supports lie in the open positive-time collar \(t\ge\delta\).
Use regulated reflection positivity: \(Q_{a,L}(F^\delta,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_jS_{a,L}((\Theta F_i^\delta)^*F_j^\delta)\ge0\).

Invoke the fixed-collar part of the RG limit. Because the reflected supports are separated by distance \(2\delta\), the limiting topology is assumed strong enough to pass this finite quadratic form: \(Q_{a,L}(F^\delta,c)\to Q_S(F^\delta,c)\). Hence \(Q_S(F^\delta,c)\ge0\).

For \(F_i\) in the mirror-smooth core, represent each reflected product by a full-space test tensor \(\Phi_{ij,\delta}\). The geometry is chosen so that \(\Phi_{ij,\delta}\to\Phi_{ij,0}\) in the same test topology on which \(S\) is continuous.
Apply distributional continuity termwise: \(S(\Phi_{ij,\delta})\to S(\Phi_{ij,0})\), hence \(Q_S(F^\delta,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\). Since every \(Q_S(F^\delta,c)\ge0\), the limit gives \(Q_S(F,c)\ge0\).

To extend beyond the mirror-smooth core, one would need to prove that every locked positive-time gauge-invariant observable is the OS-seminorm limit of mirror-smooth observables, with no extra boundary renormalization. This is precisely where cusp loops, intersection loops, and local curvature contact terms must be controlled.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is valid on a declared mirror-smooth core under continuity assumptions, but Yang-Mills existence needs the full gauge-invariant OS test algebra. Without an OS-density theorem and a no-boundary-defect theorem, the argument could silently replace the target theory by a boundary-renormalized one.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: boundary trace modulus and same-theory obstruction

assumptions: For each cutoff \((a,L)\), reflection positivity holds on the regulated gauge-invariant algebra: \(Q_{a,L}(G,c)\ge0\) for all \(G_i\in\mathcal A_{a,+}\).
For each fixed collar \(\delta>0\), the RG/cutoff-removal topology controls the reflected probe: \(Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\).
The family \(F_i\) belongs either to the full locked algebra or to a declared core that is later proved OS-dense in the full algebra.
Trace modulus: for every finite \((F,c)\), there exists \(\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\downarrow0\) such that \(|Q_S(T_\delta F,c)-Q_S(F,c)|\le\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\).
The trace modulus is same-theory: it is not achieved by rescaling observables with a boundary factor or by adding a reflection-plane defect functional.
definitions: source object: a directed family \((S_{a,L},\mathcal A_{a,+},\iota_{a,L})\) of finite-cutoff gauge-invariant Schwinger forms, each satisfying regulated reflection positivity on the same abstract positive-time observable labels after embedding \(\iota_{a,L}:\mathcal A_+\to\mathcal A_{a,+}\).

target object: a continuum gauge-invariant Schwinger functional \(S\) on the locked positive-time algebra \(mathcal A_+\), equipped with the OS quadratic form \(Q_S(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S((\Theta F_i)^*F_j)\), from which the reconstructed physical Hilbert space and positive Hamiltonian would be obtained.

controlled interface: the finite reflected quadratic forms \(Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\) for collar translations \(T_\delta\) moving supports a distance \(\delta>0\) away from the reflection plane, together with the boundary trace limit \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\).

same-theory condition: the embeddings, collar translations, and renormalization maps commute in the OS seminorm up to errors vanishing as \(a\to0,L\to\infty,\delta\downarrow0\), and no \(\delta\)-dependent boundary counterterm, cusp factor, plane observable, or changed Wilson-loop normalization is introduced at the reflection plane.

equations.label: fixed-collar positivity transfer
equations.latex: Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\ge 0,\qquad Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\longrightarrow Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\ge0
equations.valid_when: Valid for each fixed \(\delta>0\) when the cutoff-removal topology includes the reflected finite quadratic form determined by the collar-separated observables.

equations.label: boundary trace modulus
equations.valid_when: Valid only if reflected products approaching the plane have no uncancelled contact, cusp, or boundary-renormalization defect.

equations.label: OS positivity by collar limit
equations.valid_when: Valid after fixed-collar positivity and the same-theory trace modulus have both been established for the chosen finite family.

equations.label: same-theory commutator condition
equations.valid_when: Valid when the cutoff observable embedding and the collar displacement represent the same continuum gauge-invariant observable, not two differently renormalized theories.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any observable family for which \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\) has a finite but nonzero boundary defect, a divergent cusp renormalization, or a limit depending on an added plane counterterm; then the collar proof is valid only for a modified theory, not for the locked Yang-Mills algebra.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the bridge lemma that converts the already-formal closed-cone argument into a usable OS positivity passage: first prove positivity away from the reflection plane, then take a controlled same-theory boundary trace.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Boundary-defect-free collar trace bridge. Let \(S_{a,L}\) be regulated reflection-positive Schwinger functionals on a locked gauge-invariant positive-time algebra \(\mathcal A_+\), and suppose \(S_{a,L}\to S\) in a cutoff-removal topology that is valid for every fixed positive collar. If, for every finite family \(F_1,\ldots,F_N\in\mathcal A_+\) and coefficients \(c\in\mathbb C^N\), the collar translations \(T_\delta F_i\) satisfy a trace modulus \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), with no new reflection-plane renormalization, then \(S\) is OS-positive on \(\mathcal A_+\). If the estimate first holds on a core \(\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{core}}\), it extends to the full algebra exactly when that core is dense for the resulting OS seminorm without changing the observable identifications.

assumptions: The continuum local Schwinger distributions satisfy distributional continuity on the full-space nuclear test topology used by the RG limit.
For local composite fields, the same renormalized composite labels \(\mathcal O_\alpha\) are used before and after the collar limit.
For Wilson observables in the core, the loop renormalization constants do not acquire an extra angle-dependent or intersection-dependent factor at \(t=0\).
Finite products of the selected local and loop observables remain in the domain of \(S\).
definitions: \(\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{ms}}\): positive-time gauge-invariant observables whose reflected products at \(\delta=0\) are represented by ordinary full-space test objects, not by singular boundary objects.
Mirror-smooth local field condition: each smearing tensor has an extension-by-reflection or extension-by-zero that is smooth enough for the declared Schwinger distribution topology.

Mirror-smooth Wilson condition: the union \(\Theta\ell\cup\ell\) obtained at the plane is in the same loop-renormalization class as the separated pair \(\Theta T_\delta\ell\cup T_\delta\ell\), with no cusp anomaly or intersection mixing.
Continuity hypothesis: the Schwinger functional is a continuous multilinear distribution on the test topology in which the reflected test tensors converge as \(\delta\downarrow0\).

equations.label: test-tensor convergence
equations.valid_when: Valid for mirror-smooth local smearings or loop probes whose reflected doubles do not create a new singular stratum at the plane.

equations.label: distributional trace bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when \(S\) is continuous for a seminorm \(p_{ij}\) controlling the reflected test-tensor convergence.

equations.label: finite quadratic estimate
equations.valid_when: Valid for finite families from \(\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{ms}}\) after expanding the reflected quadratic form into finitely many controlled Schwinger distribution pairings.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a Wilson loop whose collar limit touches the plane has \(\langle W_{\Theta T_\delta\ell}W_{T_\delta\ell}\rangle\sim Z_{\mathrm{cusp}}(\delta,\theta)\langle W_{\Theta\ell}W_\ell\rangle\) with \(Z_{\mathrm{cusp}}\not\to1\), this lemma is false for that loop class and becomes a concrete falsifier for the same-theory passage.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This supplies a plausible dense-core source for the trace modulus and separates benign boundary approach from genuinely Yang-Mills-specific singularities.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Mirror-smooth core trace estimate. Let \(\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{ms}}\) be the gauge-invariant core generated by smeared local curvature composites \(\mathcal O_\alpha(\phi)=\int \operatorname{tr}P_\alpha(F_A,D_AF_A,\ldots)\phi\) whose extensions across \(t=0\) are smooth, together with Wilson-loop observables whose reflected double has no new cusp or intersection at the reflection plane. If the continuum Schwinger distributions are continuous on the corresponding full-space test tensors and the renormalized Wilson-loop functionals are continuous under this mirror-smooth deformation, then \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\) for all finite \((F,c)\subset\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{ms}}\).

assumptions: The fixed-collar positivity result remains true for every \(�delta>0\).
The anomalous factor or defect appears only in the approach to the reflection plane, not in the collar-separated RG convergence.
The boundary-renormalized form differs from the original locked observable form.
definitions: Boundary factor: a \(\delta\)-dependent multiplicative or mixing renormalization appearing only when reflected supports collide with the plane.
Plane defect: an additive functional supported on \(t=0\) in the limit of reflected quadratic forms.
Locked algebra: the predeclared gauge-invariant test algebra whose labels and renormalizations are fixed independently of reflection positivity.
Obstruction: failure of the map \(F\mapsto\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}T_\delta F\) to be the identity in the OS seminorm of the intended theory.

equations.label: anomalous collar asymptotic
equations.valid_when: Valid as an obstruction model when OPE/contact or cusp analysis produces a nontrivial reflection-plane contribution.

equations.label: same-theory failure criterion
equations.valid_when: Valid as a falsifier when the intended unrenormalized boundary value \(Q_S(F,c)\) is already defined in the locked algebra.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a curvature-composite OPE term or Wilson-loop cusp/intersection anomalous dimension localized at the reflection plane; that is the sharp falsifier for the proposed bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma names what would invalidate the branch: not loss of positivity in the collar, but positivity attaching to the wrong boundary-value theory.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Boundary anomaly obstruction lemma. Suppose there exists a finite gauge-invariant family \((F,c)\) for which the collar limit exists only after a nontrivial boundary renormalization, or has a residual plane defect: \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)=Z_{F,c}(\delta)Q_S^{\mathrm{bdry-ren}}(F,c)+B_{F,c}+o(1)\), with \(Z_{F,c}\not\to1\) or \(B_{F,c}\ne0\). Then the closed-cone positivity transfer does not prove OS positivity for the original continuum Yang-Mills Schwinger functions on the locked algebra; it proves at most positivity for a modified boundary-renormalized algebra.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this route if a standard Wilson-loop cusp/intersection or curvature-composite OPE calculation forces a nontrivial reflection-plane factor for observables that must belong to the locked OS algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the lemma if one proves: (1) fixed-collar RG convergence for reflected probes; (2) mirror-smooth core trace modulus; (3) OS-density of that core in the locked gauge-invariant algebra; and (4) no boundary counterterm or cusp factor in the collar limit.
control_decision.reason: The branch remains productive because it has moved from a tautological closed-cone argument to a falsifiable boundary trace theorem with explicit Yang-Mills obstructions. The next work should test the mirror-smooth core and cusp/contact falsifiers rather than rename the topology.

falsifiers: Cusp-loop falsifier: choose a family of positive-time Wilson loops \(\ell_\delta=T_\delta\ell\) whose reflected double develops a cusp or intersection at \(t=0\); if the continuum expectation contains a nontrivial \(Z_{\mathrm{cusp}}(\delta,\theta)\), the trace modulus is not same-theory valid.

Curvature-contact falsifier: take smeared \(\operatorname{tr}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}\) observables whose supports approach the plane; if the OPE of \((\Theta O)O\) produces a surviving \(\delta(t)\)-supported counterterm, collar positivity does not transfer to the original OS form.

Topology falsifier: the Balaban/RG convergence topology controls only separated ordinary Schwinger distributions but not the reflected tensors \(\Phi_{ij,\delta}\) uniformly as \(\delta\downarrow0\). Then fixed-collar closedness is valid but boundary passage is unproved.

Algebra-change falsifier: if the proof obtains continuity only after restricting to mirror-smooth observables and this core is not OS-dense in the locked algebra, the resulting positivity is for a smaller theory.

Renormalization-commutator falsifier: if \(\iota_{a,L}T_\delta F\) and \(T_\delta\iota_{a,L}F\) have different limiting renormalization constants near the plane, the source and target objects are not the same theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 175 turns the trace-modulus slogan into a concrete two-layer program. The positivity passage is valid and short once \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\) is known, but that estimate is exactly where Yang-Mills singular geometry enters. A mirror-smooth gauge-invariant core gives a plausible route because ordinary distributional continuity can prove the trace limit there. The real discovery is the obstruction criterion: cusp anomalous factors, curvature contact terms, or boundary counterterms are not minor technicalities; any one is a falsifier of the same-theory bridge. Thus the branch has isolated a precise analytic target: prove no-new-boundary-renormalization plus OS-density of the mirror-smooth core, or exhibit a concrete cusp/contact counterexample.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out one model boundary calculation: take a local gauge-invariant curvature composite smeared by \(\phi(t,x)\) with \(\phi\) nonflat at \(t=0\), compute the expected OPE scaling of \(S((\Theta T_\delta O_\phi)O_{T_\delta\phi})\), and determine whether the singular terms pair to an ordinary distributional limit or require a plane-supported subtraction. In parallel, formulate the analogous Wilson-loop test for a reflected double developing a cusp at the plane.
